arxiv-1809-00828.title: Robust and parallel scalable iterative solutions for large-scale finite cell analyses
arxiv-1809-00828.creator: J. N. Jomo, F. de Prenter, M. Elhaddad, D. D’Angella, C. V. Verhoosel, S. Kollmannsberger, J. S. Kirschke, V. Nübel, E. H. van Brummelen, E. Rank
arxiv-1809-00828.description: Abstract Abstract The finite cell method is a highly flexible discretization technique for numerical analysis on domains with complex geometries. By using a non-boundary conforming computational domain that can be easily meshed, automatized computations on a wide range of geometrical models can be performed.

arxiv-2109-12768.title: Growth of Outward Propagating Fast-Magnetosonic/Whistler Waves in the Inner Heliosphere Observed by Parker Solar Probe
arxiv-2109-12768.creator: Jiansen He, Ying Wang, Xingyu Zhu, Die Duan, Daniel Verscharen, Guoqing Zhao
arxiv-2109-12768.description: Abstract The solar wind in the inner heliosphere has been observed by Parker Solar Probe ( PSP ) to exhibit abundant wave activities. The cyclotron wave modes in the sense of ions or electrons are among the most crucial wave components. However, their origin and evolution in the inner heliosphere close to the Sun remain mysteries.

arxiv-2111-01697.title: Low-Rank+Sparse Tensor Compression for Neural Networks
arxiv-2111-01697.creator: Cole Hawkins, Haichuan Yang, Meng Li, Liangzhen Lai, Vikas Chandra
arxiv-2111-01697.description: Abstract Low-rank tensor compression has been proposed as a promising approach to reduce the memory and compute requirements of neural networks for their deployment on edge devices. Tensor compression reduces the number of parameters required to represent a neural network weight by assuming network weights possess a coarse higher-order structure.

arxiv-2301-10852.title: Flexagon: A Multi-Dataflow Sparse-Sparse Matrix Multiplication Accelerator for Efficient DNN Processing
arxiv-2301-10852.creator: Francisco Muñoz-Martínez ∗ Raveesh Garg † José L. Abellán ∗ Manuel E. Acacio ∗ Tushar Krishna † Michael Pellauer ‡ ∗ Universidad de Murcia, † Georgia Tech, ‡ NVIDIA Contact author: francisco.munoz2@um.es

Existing Sparse-Sparse Matrix Multiplication (SpMSpM) accelerators are tailored to a particular SpMSpM dataflow (i.e., Inner Product, Outer Product or Gustavson’s), that determines their overall efficiency. arxiv-2303-12971.title: Differentiable hybrid neural modeling for fluid-structure interaction Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2303-12971.creator: Xiantao Fan, Jian-xun Wang
arxiv-2303-12971.description: Abstract Solving complex fluid-structure interaction (FSI) problems, which are described by nonlinear partial differential equations, is crucial in various scientific and engineering applications. Traditional computational fluid dynamics based solvers are inadequate to handle the increasing demand for large-scale and long-period simulations.

arxiv-2310-20127.title: Improving Prompt Tuning with Learned Prompting Layers
arxiv-2310-20127.creator: Wei Zhu, Ming Tan
arxiv-2310-20127.description: Abstract Prompt tuning prepends a soft prompt to the input embeddings or hidden states and only optimizes the prompt to adapt pretrained models (PTMs) to downstream tasks. The previous work manually selects prompt layers which are far from optimal and failed to exploit the potential of prompt tuning.

arxiv-2412-08506.title: Orchestrating the Symphony of Prompt Distribution Learning for Human-Object Interaction Detection
arxiv-2412-08506.creator: Mingda Jia, Liming Zhao, Ge Li, Yun Zheng
arxiv-2412-08506.description: Abstract Human-object interaction (HOI) detectors with popular query-transformer architecture have achieved promising performance. However, accurately identifying uncommon visual patterns and distinguishing between ambiguous HOIs continue to be difficult for them. We observe that these difficulties may arise from the limited capacity of traditional detector queries in representing diverse intra-category patterns and inter-category dependencies.

arxiv-2412-11715.title: Discrepancy-Aware Attention Network for Enhanced Audio-Visual Zero-Shot Learning Thanks: † Equally contributions *Corresponding author.

arxiv-2412-11715.description: Abstract Audio-visual Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) has attracted significant attention for its ability to identify unseen classes and perform well in video classification tasks. However, modal imbalance in (G)ZSL leads to over-reliance on the optimal modality, reducing discriminative capabilities for unseen classes.

arxiv-2511-01701.title: Solution Space Topology Guides CMTS Search
arxiv-2511-01701.creator: Mirco A. Mannucci
arxiv-2511-01701.description: Abstract A fundamental question in search-guided AI: what topology should guide Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) in puzzle solving? Prior work applied topological features to guide MCTS in ARC-style tasks using grid topology—the Laplacian spectral properties of cell connectivity—and found no benefit. We identify the root cause: grid topology is constant across all instances.

arxiv-2601-09510.title: Powers in prime bases and a problem on central binomial coefficients
arxiv-2601-09510.creator: Sebastian Tim Holdum, Frederik Ravn Klausen, Peter Michael Reichstein Rasmussen
arxiv-2601-09510.description: Abstract Abstract It is an open problem whether \binom{2n}{n} is divisible by 4 or 9 for all n>256 . In connection with this, we prove that for a fixed uneven m the asymptotic density of k ’s such that m\nmid\binom{2^{k+1}}{2^{k}} is 0.

pmc-13270549.title: Cognitive performance recovery following marijuana cessation in NCAA division I athletes
pmc-13270549.creator: Brandon A. Ally, Paul A. Mentele, Scott A. Wylie
pmc-13270549.description: BackgroundCannabis use is increasingly common among collegiate athletes. While acute tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) effects are well documented, the chronic impact on game-speed cognition, defined as the ability to perceive, decide, and act within sub-second windows, remains poorly quantified.
